name: Cylinder head
what: The DOHC cylinder head closes the cylinders and carries the combustion chambers, four-valve-per-cylinder layout, intake and exhaust ports, camshaft bearing structures, spark-plug wells, and coolant and oil passages.
why: It forms the upper combustion-chamber surfaces and supports the valvetrain that controls gas exchange. Its ports and passages route intake charge, exhaust gas, coolant, and lubricating oil.
where: It mounts to the block over the head gasket. The combustion chambers face the pistons; the camshaft and valve hardware mount on the upper side.
installationReason: Lower the cylinder head onto the installed gasket, keeping the combustion chambers and fluid passages aligned with the block.

guide.overview: The B16 cylinder head is an aluminum-alloy DOHC, four-valve-per-cylinder casting. It forms the roof of each combustion chamber and contains the intake and exhaust ports, valve guides and seats, spark-plug wells, camshaft bearing supports, and oil and coolant passages.
guide.operation: The intake and exhaust valves are actuated by the twin camshafts through the valvetrain. The intake ports feed the cylinders, combustion occurs between the head chambers and piston crowns, and exhaust ports route spent gases away. Coolant circulates through water jackets, while pressurized oil feeds the camshaft and valvetrain areas.
guide.construction: The teaching model distinguishes the main aluminum casting, machined deck, four combustion-chamber areas, valve-seat locations, twin camshaft support rails, spark-plug wells, port flanges, head-bolt bosses, and external casting ribs.
